recommended_title_en: Two-Track Safety-Gated Inference for Risk-Control Decision Support

paragraphs: This work addresses a governance problem in systems that derive dense, meaning-rich signals from cross-reference knowledge networks. Such signals are expressive but prone to overfitting and false discovery when promoted directly into operational decisions. We therefore frame the task as a promotion-control problem where narrative insight and operational claims must be separated.

Our contribution is an engineering architecture and reproducibility stack rather than a market-direction oracle. We separate K-track (knowledge/research lane) from T-track (operational survivorship and rollback lane), and evaluate under artifact-anchored protocol: benchmark comparison, raw OOS readiness checks, bootstrap/permutation significance, and falsification suite scans.

Empirically, current as-of artifacts indicate bundle readiness and publication-claim readiness under defined test conditions. Statistical reports support positive delta interpretation, and falsification checks pass with reviewer-facing first-break disclosure at survivor threshold 7. We emphasize bounded interpretation and protocol transparency over headline directional claims.

Disclosure posture: Public-safe disclosure only. Core formula/weight internals remain redacted, and high-complexity historical corpora are treated as stress-test beds for context-filter robustness rather than doctrinal proof. The narrative focus is safety gates, rollback contracts, reproducible artifacts, and lane separation.

Fail-boundary disclosure: maximum safe survivor-floor observed in sensitivity grid is 5, and first break condition appears at survivor-floor 7. We use this boundary as an explicit reviewer-facing risk condition.

Title for submission packaging: "Two-Track Safety-Gated Inference for Risk-Control Decision Support". Limitations include domain-specific semantics, snapshot dependence, and the need for extended drift windows; we provide replication via referenced artifacts and scripts rather than proprietary tuning tables.

compressed_abstracts_en.kdd_180w: We present a two-track safety-gated inference architecture for risk-control operations over meaning-rich cross-reference signals. The system separates K-track (knowledge/research lane) from T-track (operational survivorship and rollback lane) to prevent direct promotion of overfit signals into operations. Claims are artifact-anchored and reproducible through multi-baseline comparison, raw OOS readiness checks, bootstrap/permutation significance, and falsification boundary scans. Current as-of artifacts indicate bundle readiness and publication-claim readiness under tested conditions; significance supports positive delta, and falsification reports first non-pass at survivor threshold 7. A fail-boundary layer sets max-safe survivor floor at 5 and first-break at 7 for explicit no-go semantics. Historical corpora are treated as stress-test beds for context-filter robustness, not doctrinal proof. The system prioritizes risk-off governance, auditability, and reproducibility over directional market claims.
compressed_abstracts_en.aaai_150w: We introduce a deployment-oriented safety-gated inference stack for narrative-heavy systems. K-track knowledge generation is isolated from T-track operational gating, and promotion claims require benchmark, raw OOS, significance, and falsification evidence. Under current as-of artifacts, bundle/readiness gates are satisfied under tested conditions, significance supports positive delta, and boundary analysis reports first non-pass at survivor threshold 7 with rollback/no-go semantics. The paper emphasizes auditable artifact trails and bounded interpretation while keeping proprietary formula internals redacted. Product mapping remains split by design: Macro Risk Warning API for operational governance and Logos Resonance Explorer API for research exploration. Outputs are intended for risk-control observability, not guaranteed directional return claims.
